title: Elon Musk says Starlink integration could expand to other Tesla models by late 2027
html:
Tesla could begin bringing built-in Starlink connectivity to more of its vehicles by late 2027. The technology, which made its debut in the Cybercab earlier this year, could eventually expand across Tesla’s broader lineup as the company moves toward unsupervised Full Self-Driving (FSD).

The update came in response to a post on X, who said he was looking forward to Tesla offering an embedded Starlink option in all models beyond the Cybercab.

Musk replied, “Hopefully available towards the end of next year.”

He also explained why the technology will become increasingly important as Tesla moves toward unsupervised autonomous driving.

“This will be important for unsupervised FSD, so passengers have high bandwidth everywhere for work and entertainment.”

It is worth noting that this will be an easier task than it was earlier this year. Given the company’s recent decisions to shrink its lineup of consumer passenger vehicles from 5 down to 2, this means Tesla will only have to integrate Starlink into the Model 3 and Model Y.

Why add Starlink?

Musk has also previously explained why Starlink is particularly important for Tesla’s autonomous vehicles. During the company’s Q2 2026 earnings call, he said Tesla couldn’t have Robotaxis getting stuck in areas without cellular coverage, describing them as “Bermuda Triangles of lack of cellular connectivity.”

Starlink provides an alternative connection when cellular networks are unavailable, but Musk’s latest comments highlight another important benefit: the passenger experience.

With unsupervised FSD, occupants would no longer need to monitor the road, allowing them to spend their time working, watching movies, or using other online services. Having high-speed internet available throughout the journey would make those activities possible even in areas with limited cellular coverage.

Cybercab was the first Tesla with Starlink

Tesla’s plans for integrated satellite connectivity aren’t new. Back in August, the company confirmed that the Cybercab would be its first vehicle equipped with built-in Starlink, sharing photos of the hardware neatly integrated into the rear of the autonomous two-seater.

Before that confirmation, prototype Cybercabs had been spotted with what appeared to be Starlink equipment mounted externally, suggesting Tesla was already testing the technology.
summary: Elon Musk says Tesla hopes to begin offering integrated Starlink connectivity in other models by late 2027, expanding beyond the Cybercab.
